controls: fresh random import as a floor

decision_criteria.PHENOMENON_ABSENT: no import kind takes over (dose too small / no selection gradient)
decision_criteria.PHENOMENON_CHANGED/INVERTED: mature takes over substantially more than permuted (competence DOES drive takeover in BEE)
decision_criteria.PHENOMENON_PRESERVED: mature and permuted reach a similar final import-share (takeover is dose-driven, as C3-SFE-10)

imports.mature: best elite of a 10-generation search on the world

prereg.initial_state: generation 0 = DOSE copies of the import (origin=import) + fresh residents

entries.bee: seed_players injected into generation 0 with origin=import (the S3 scaffolding)
entries.reason: injected players take the first slots of generation 0; their descendants inherit the origin
entries.source: a mature organism injected into a population

entries.bee: fraction of archive elites with origin=import, per generation
entries.reason: origin travels through player meta, so the archive records import vs resident lineage per generation
entries.source: the import lineage's share of the population over time

entries.bee: best elite of a prior search on the same world
entries.reason: matured by BEE's own search rather than the source's, but on the same world
entries.source: an organism matured on the world

entries.bee: transform.shuffle.v1 of the mature elite (permutes the table)
entries.reason: the shuffle keeps the components and complexity but scrambles the behaviour -- the permuted control
entries.source: the import scrambled (same material, no competence)

entries.bee: seed_players = DOSE DISTINCT organisms of the kind (top-DOSE elites for mature; their individual shuffles for permuted; DOSE randoms for fresh)
entries.reason: BEE's sweep forbids duplicate players (every population member must be distinct), so a dose of byte-identical clones is UNREPRESENTABLE; the dose is DOSE distinct organisms of the same kind
BEE's search has no per-parent offspring cap; takeover is shaped by selection, not a quota
hill-climb on charge; a competent import should out-select residents, a scrambled one should not

observations: import-origin share of the archive per generation
prereg.question: Does a MATURE import take over a population more than its PERMUTED control (a scrambled copy)? If they take over equally, takeover is driven by the dose/injection, not by competence (as C3-SFE-10).
prereg.stopping_rules: fixed budget; equal takeover of mature and permuted is the CAPABLE_NEGATIVE result, not a failure
